sentences.text: Padalarenuka vs State Of Telangana on 16 April, 2024

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.16 of 2020
Order:

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue an appropriate writ order or directions more particularly one of the nature of writ of Mandamus declaring in action of the respondent No.5 in sending the requisite proposal for payment of compensation to the respondent No.4 in respect of the land of the petitioner admeasuring Ac.0-14 guntas in Sy.No.219 of Kanteshwar shivar, Nizamabad acquired for laying the Bypass road from Kanteshwar to Arsapally, Nizamabad as illegal, arbitrary and violative of Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondent No.5 to send the requisite proposal for payment of compensation in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.0.14 guntas in Sy.No.219 of Kanteshwar shivar, Nizamabad belonging to the Petitioner to the respondent No.4 and pass..."
2.

Heard Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings appearing for the respondents and perused the entire material on record.
SK,J 3.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that an extent of Ac.0.14 guntas of land of the petitioner in Sy.No.219, situated at Kanteshwar Shivar, Nizamabad was acquired by the Respondent Nos.3 to 5 for formation of Bypass road.
The land acquisition proposal for the Bypass road was already approved and payments were made as per norms.
However, in the said proposal the land of the petitioner was not mentioned but, was acquired without paying any compensation to the petitioner.

Basing on the application made by the petitioner, the official respondents conducted survey and demarcation and stated that the land to an extent of Ac.0-14 guntas of the petitioner in Sy.No.219 was acquired for laying the Bypass Road out of Ac.0.22 guntas.

The Respondent No.4 has addressed a letter to the Respondent No.5 in letter No.B2/1549/2009, dated 06.10.2016 for sending the requisition proposal for payment of the land acquisition compensation to the SK,J petitioner.

In turn, the respondent No.5 addressed letter to the respondent No.4 stating that after 5 years of formation of the road and acquisition, it is not possible either to demarcate or submit the proposal.

In view of the same, the respondent No.4 is unable to pay compensation to the petitioner and also addressed letter to the respondent No.5 on 29.05.2017 and once again asked the respondent No.5 to initiate land acquisition proceedings for payment of land acquisition compensation to the petitioner on 23.08.2019.
In spite of that, the respondent No.5 is not taking any action.

Unless the respondent No.5 sent a requisition proposal, the respondent No.4 cannot determine the compensation amount payable to the petitioner and the petitioner is unable to get compensation to the land acquired by Padalarenuka vs State Of Telangana on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18284924/
1 the respondents and requested to direct the respondents to take necessary steps to pay the land acquisition SK,J compensation to the petitioner and allow the writ petition.
4. Learned Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.5 basing on the counter submits that the respondent No.5 has no knowledge about the ownership of the petitioner's land.

The formation of the Bypass Road in Nizamabad Town administratively sanctioned in the year, 2008 by the then Government in G.O.Ms.No.1438, T, R&B (RIII) Department, dated 23.09.2008 for Rs.5000.00 Lakhs.

A draft notification was issued Under Section 4 (1) of Land Acquisition Act and after completion of the land acquisition process, compensation was paid to the owners of the land between the years, 2013 to 2015.

The total extent of land published in DN & DD (patta land) is Ac.7.08 guntas and Ac.0.09 guntas of Government land, out of which Ac.7.05 guntas compensation was made to respective land owners as per publication and also additional land to an SK,J extent of Ac.01.01/2 guntas also paid in Kanteshwar Shivar.
Entire compensation amount was deposited with the LAO, Nizamabad.
But there was a problem with the land of Ac.0.3 guntas.
The Compensation of 0.3 guntas is lying with the LAO, Nizamabad.
Therefore the question of sending proposals of additional land for Ac.0.014 guntas does not arise and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

5. After hearing both sides and perusing the entire material on record, this Court is of the considered view that the respondent-authorities have initiated land acquisition proceedings for formation of Bypass Road in Nizamabad Town and acquired land to an extent of Ac.88.35  guntas vide Collector proceedings No.G1/3079/2009, dated 06.07.2010 and accordingly, the R&B Department deposited an amount of Rs.35,42,90,000/- before the respondent No.4 for acquired land.
SK,J 6.

At the time of formation of the road, the land of the petitioner to an extent of Ac.0.14 guntas in Sy.No.219, situated at Kanteshwar Shivar, Nizamabad was taken over by the official respondents without initiating any land acquisition proceedings.
Basing on the representation filed by the petitioner, the respondent No.4 conducted survey and demarcation.

The respondent No.7 submitted report to the respondent No.4 on 27.07.2016 and in the said report, it was clearly stated that an extent of Ac.0.14 guntas of land of the petitioner in Sy.No.219, situated at Kanteshwar Shivar,
Nizamabad
was acquired for laying Bypass Road out of Ac.0.22 guntas.

In spite of several reminders of the respondent No.4 for payment of compensation for the land of the petitioner which was acquired for the formation of road, the respondent No.5 is not taking any action and stating that the land acquisition proceedings was completed and payment were also made to others SK,J and the question of further initiation of land acquisition does not arise and no action is taken in this regard.

7. The respondent No.5 had nowhere disputed the survey conducted by the respondent No.7 in his counter and not initiated land acquisition proceedings on the ground that the payment for land acquisition compensation was completed and amounts were deposited to the respondent No.4.
8.

Once the competent authority i.e., The Deputy Inspector, Survey and Demarcation, Survey and Land Records, Nizamabad conducted survey and submitted his report and stating that the land of the petitioner was acquired for the formation of Bypass Road.

It is the duty of the respondents to Padalarenuka vs State Of Telangana on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18284924/
2 pay the land acquisition compensation to the petitioners as per the Land Acquisition Act

. 
SK,J 9.

In view of the above findings, the writ petition is disposed of by directing the respondent Nos.4 and 5 to initiate land acquisition proceedings for payment of compensation in respect of the land of the petitioner admeasuring Ac.0-14 guntas in Sy.No.219 of Kanteshwar shivar, Nizamabad acquired for laying the Bypass Road from Kanteshwar to Arsapally, Nizamabad within two (2) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
10. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

JUSTICE K.SARATH Date: 16.04.2024 BB Padalarenuka vs State Of Telangana on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18284924/
